item.title: Work Keeps Us Busy. Food Stamps Keep Us Going: Why Florida’s largest employers and low-wage jobs rely on SNAP
item.description: In Florida and across the U.S., millions of full- and part-time workers at major companies need the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) just to feed their families. But public policy and corporate pay practices are rarely acknowledged. In 2024 more than 41.7 million Americans—roughly 12.3% of the U.S. population—relied on SNAP to put food on the table. item.title: Thomas Paine: An appreciation of America’s ‘No Kings’ hero
item.description: There is a story that the author, Thomas Paine, was so enthusiastic and excited upon receiving his printed copies that he opened up the window of his lodging and started throwing copies to people passing by in the street. The story has never been historically verified, but even if untrue, it should be true. Paine knew he had written an original and powerful work. As he foresaw, it went on to shake the American colonies and ultimately the world.

item.title: Congress Knew About Matt Gaetz. They hid the truth from the public.
item.description: In December 2024, the U.S. House Committee on Ethics completed a draft report concluding that Representative Matt Gaetz had engaged in a wide range of unethical — and in some cases illegal — conduct while serving in Congress. The report was circulated privately among committee members and staff. Not long after, Gaetz’s nomination to serve as U.S. Attorney General was quietly withdrawn. And then the report stayed hidden.
